analysis: The PR makes two one-line API-shape adaptations. MediaIngest.swift:422 changes `if case .ciImage(let ci) = image` to `image.source`, and MiMoV26EncodedMediaIngress.swift:252 changes `decoded.video` to `decoded.video.source`. Both follow an upstream MLXLMCommon UserInput.Image/Video type change from enum to wrapper struct with a `.source` property. I traced the surrounding code. The nil-header image aggregate pixel re-check (MediaIngest.swift:422-433) still runs for CIImage-backed images, since decodeImageData returns `.ciImage(image)` and `.source` exposes the same case. The MiMo video path (line 252) still requires a memory-backed owner, so non-memory-backed videos are refused via refusal(). The memory-backed asset is still retained via reservation.retainEncodedOwner. Inline-only data: URI enforcement, byte caps, pixel caps, video duration and coded-dimension limits, and the no-plaintext-temp-file design are unchanged. This is consistent with T-050 and TB-003. No new data exposure, SSRF, or file-write surface appears in the supplied source. Unverified contract: the upstream `.source` semantics (the dependency's UserInput.Image/Video definitions) are outside the supplied evidence. If `.source` could return a different case than before, such as a file-URL-backed video, the guards would fail closed (refusal) or be skipped for the image re-check. decodeVideo's return line 819 `.memoryBacked(memoryAsset)` is presumably a static factory on the new type, and I did not verify it. Integration should confirm the dependency pin and that the other call sites (EngineV2VisionPrefill and others) compile and use `.source` consistently. No security regression is identified.
